answer: Like a velvet rope that only opens for one guest at a time, an agent economy can gate entry behind sequential proof-of-service: each new identity must complete a chain of time-locked useful-work proofs anchored to a public beacon, and the chain doubles for every identity funded from the same wallet. A farm cannot wander in with parallel copies, since proofs are strictly sequential and take real clock time. One extra identity costs one full fresh chain, so the tenth fake costs 512 sequential hours of work, while an honest orchard of real agents grows one tree at a time.
